q: According to Newton's second law, an object that is accelerating must have a ____ acting on it.
e: According to Newton's second law, an object that is accelerating must have a net force acting on it. Net force is the vector sum; zero net force means constant velocity.

q: An object moving in a circle, such as a ball on the end of a string, must therefore have a force applied to it to keep it moving in the ____.
e: An object moving in a circle, such as a ball on the end of a string, must therefore have a force applied to it to keep it moving in the circle. The circular path is the one that needs a centre-seeking force, unlike a straight line.

q: This force applied to keep an object moving in a circle is known as the ____ force.
e: This force applied to keep an object moving in a circle is known as the centripetal force. Centripetal means toward the centre of the circle.

q: For uniform circular motion, the acceleration is centripetal acceleration which is directed towards the ____ of the circle at any moment.
e: For uniform circular motion, the acceleration is centripetal acceleration which is directed towards the centre of the circle at any moment. The centre of the circle is where a_C and F_c point.

q: According to Newton's second law, an object in a circular motion requires a net force directed towards the ____ of the circle.
e: According to Newton's second law, an object in a circular motion requires a net force directed towards the centre of the circle. The centre of the circle is where a_C and F_c point.

q: In the absence of centripetal force, the object would not move along a circle but move in a , according to Newton's first law.
e: The blank is straight line. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r. That word is the one that completes the idea about absence centripetal force object move along.

q: For an object to move in a circle, a force is needed to deviate from its straight line path and ____ towards the centre of the circle.
e: For an object to move in a circle, a force is needed to deviate from its straight line path and accelerate towards the centre of the circle. A changing velocity, including a turning one, means the object accelerates.

q: To swing a ball on the end of a string in a circle, we pull on the string and the string exerts the force () on the ball.
e: The blank is tension. String tension can be the inward centripetal force on a whirling ball. That word is the one that completes the idea about swing ball end string circle pull.

q: The ____ in the string provides the required centripetal force for the ball to keep moving in a circular path.
e: The tension in the string provides the required centripetal force for the ball to keep moving in a circular path. String tension can be the inward centripetal force on a whirling ball.

q: The gravitational force of the earth on the ____ orbiting the earth is an example of a centripetal force.
e: The gravitational force of the earth on the moon orbiting the earth is an example of a centripetal force. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r.

q: The gravitational force of the sun on the ____ orbiting the sun is an example of a centripetal force.
e: The gravitational force of the sun on the planets orbiting the sun is an example of a centripetal force. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r.

q: The ____ force acting on an electron orbiting the nucleus is an example of a centripetal force.
e: The electric force acting on an electron orbiting the nucleus is an example of a centripetal force. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r.

q: When whirling a body attached to a string, a ____ force is originated.
e: When whirling a body attached to a string, a tension force is originated. String tension can be the inward centripetal force on a whirling ball.

q: If the tension force is normal to the direction of motion of a body moving at constant speed, this force causes the body to move in a ____ path.
e: If the tension force is normal to the direction of motion of a body moving at constant speed, this force causes the body to move in a circular path. Each particle of a rotor travels on a circular path about the axis.

q: An attractive force exists between the sun and the earth in a direction ____ to the path of the earth.
e: An attractive force exists between the sun and the earth in a direction perpendicular to the path of the earth. Perpendicular means the two directions stand at right angles.

q: The gravitational force causes the earth to move in a circular path around the ____.
e: The gravitational force causes the earth to move in a circular path around the sun. Gravity of the Sun on Earth is the centripetal force of the orbit.

q: The Coulomb attractive force between the nucleus and the electron acts as the required centripetal force for the electron to move around the ____.
e: The Coulomb attractive force between the nucleus and the electron acts as the required centripetal force for the electron to move around the nucleus. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r.

q: When a car turns in a circular path or a curve, a ____ force exists between the road and the car tires.
e: When a car turns in a circular path or a curve, a frictional force exists between the road and the car tires. On a level curve, frictional force of the tires supplies F_c.

q: When a car moves in a circular path which is inclined to the horizontal, the ____ force of the road acts normally to the car.
e: When a car moves in a circular path which is inclined to the horizontal, the reaction force of the road acts normally to the car. The road's reaction is the normal force, standing perpendicular to the surface.

q: Resolving this reaction force (normal force) into two components, the ____ component acts towards the centre of the circle and helps the car to move in a curved path.
e: Resolving this reaction force (normal force) into two components, the horizontal component acts towards the centre of the circle and helps the car to move in a curved path. The horizontal part of N or lift is the centripetal component on a banked path.

q: The horizontal component of ____ force is the required centripetal force for a car on an inclined circular path.
e: The horizontal component of normal force is the required centripetal force for a car on an inclined circular path. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r.

q: The upward thrust (lifting force) acts ____ to an aeroplane body.
e: The upward thrust (lifting force) acts normally to an aeroplane body. Normally means at right angles to the surface.

q: When the aeroplane tilts, the horizontal component acts normally to the motion of the aeroplane, causing the aeroplane to turn in a .
e: The blank is curve. That word is the one that completes the idea about aeroplane tilts horizontal component acts normally.

q: This means that the horizontal component of the lifting force on the aeroplane provides the ____ force.
e: This means that the horizontal component of the lifting force on the aeroplane provides the centripetal force. Centripetal means toward the centre of the circle.

q: When an automobile drives round a curve, it must have a force exerted towards the ____ of the curve.
e: When an automobile drives round a curve, it must have a force exerted towards the centre of the curve. The centre of the circle is where a_C and F_c point.

q: On a flat road ( road), the centripetal force is supplied by friction between the tires and the road.
e: The blank is unbanked. A banked track tilts so the horizontal part of the normal force can supply some or all of the centripetal requirement. That word is the one that completes the idea about flat road centripetal force supplied friction.

q: If the frictional force is not sufficient, such as under wet and slippery conditions, the car will ____ out of the circular path.
e: If the frictional force is not sufficient, such as under wet and slippery conditions, the car will skid out of the circular path. If friction cannot supply mv²/r, the car will skid out of the curve.

q: To prevent skidding, the road must be ____ to provide the necessary centripetal force to the automobiles.
e: To prevent skidding, the road must be banked to provide the necessary centripetal force to the automobiles. A banked track tilts so the horizontal part of the normal force can supply some or all of the centripetal requirement.

q: Banking of roads is raising the ____ edge of the curved road higher than the inner edge.
e: Banking of roads is raising the outer edge of the curved road higher than the inner edge. A banked track tilts so the horizontal part of the normal force can supply some or all of the centripetal requirement.

q: The angle that the inclined track makes with horizontal is called angle of ____.
e: The angle that the inclined track makes with horizontal is called angle of banking. A banked track tilts so the horizontal part of the normal force can supply some or all of the centripetal requirement.

q: The normal force exerted by a banked road is ____ to the road.
e: The normal force exerted by a banked road is perpendicular to the road. Perpendicular means the two directions stand at right angles.

q: For every banked curve, there is a ____ speed at which the entire centripetal force is supplied by the horizontal component of the normal force.
e: For every banked curve, there is a limiting speed at which the entire centripetal force is supplied by the horizontal component of the normal force. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r.

q: At the limiting speed on a banked curve, the ____ force between the tires and the road is not required.
e: At the limiting speed on a banked curve, the frictional force between the tires and the road is not required. On a level curve, frictional force of the tires supplies F_c.

q: In circular motion, there are two different ____ that are encountered.
e: In circular motion, there are two different forces that are encountered. Several real forces can add to give the net centripetal requirement.

q: They are centripetal force and ____ force.
e: They are centripetal force and centrifugal force. Centrifugal names the apparent outward effect in the rotating frame.

q: Centripetal force is the force acting towards the centre of the circular path, whereas the centrifugal force appears to act in a direction pointing ____ from the centre.
e: Centripetal force is the force acting towards the centre of the circular path, whereas the centrifugal force appears to act in a direction pointing away from the centre. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r.

q: Consider, for example, a person whirls a ball on the end of a string in a horizontal circle around his ____.
e: Consider, for example, a person whirls a ball on the end of a string in a horizontal circle around his head. Head is the elevation difference that sets the gravitational potential of the water.

q: The person pulls the string to exert an ____ force on the ball.
e: The person pulls the string to exert an inward force on the ball. Inward is toward the centre, the real centripetal sense.

q: According to Newton's third law, the ball exerts a ____ force on the hand.
e: According to Newton's third law, the ball exerts a reaction force on the hand. The road's reaction is the normal force, standing perpendicular to the surface.

q: There is a misconception that this reaction force is the outward-directed ____ force acting on the ball.
e: There is a misconception that this reaction force is the outward-directed centrifugal force acting on the ball. Centrifugal names the apparent outward effect in the rotating frame.

q: Except centripetal force, there is no other force acting on the ball along the ____.
e: Except centripetal force, there is no other force acting on the ball along the string. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r.

q: When a car is moving with constant velocity along a straight road, there is no ____ force on the person.
e: When a car is moving with constant velocity along a straight road, there is no net force on the person. Net force is the vector sum; zero net force means constant velocity.

q: However, when the car moves around a curve the person feels an ____ force exerted on him.
e: However, when the car moves around a curve the person feels an outward force exerted on him. Outward is away from the centre, the apparent centrifugal sense.

q: Actually, the centrifugal force is not a ____ force.
e: Actually, the centrifugal force is not a real force. Centrifugal force is not a real interaction; it is an apparent outward effect of inertia in the rotating frame.

q: It is an apparent or ____ force which is equal and opposite to the centripetal force.
e: It is an apparent or fictitious force which is equal and opposite to the centripetal force. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r.

q: Although centrifugal force is not a real force, the concept can be applied in rotating devices, such as centrifuges, washing machines, centrifugal pumps, centrifugal governors and centrifugal ____.
e: The blank is clutches. Centrifugal force is not a real interaction; it is an apparent outward effect of inertia in the rotating frame. That word is the one that completes the idea about Although centrifugal force real concept applied.

q: A centrifuge is a piece of equipment that puts an object in rotation around a fixed ____.
e: A centrifuge is a piece of equipment that puts an object in rotation around a fixed axis. Rotational motion means a body spins about an axis.

q: In a laboratory centrifuge, the radial acceleration causes denser particles to settle to the ____ of the tube.
e: In a laboratory centrifuge, the radial acceleration causes denser particles to settle to the bottom of the tube. A centrifuge spins samples about a fixed axis so radial acceleration separates materials by density.

q: In a laboratory centrifuge, low density substances rise to the ____ of the tube.
e: In a laboratory centrifuge, low density substances rise to the top of the tube. A centrifuge spins samples about a fixed axis so radial acceleration separates materials by density.

q: The effect of denser particles settling and low density substances rising in a centrifuge is known as the ____ principle.
e: The effect of denser particles settling and low density substances rising in a centrifuge is known as the sedimentation principle. Sedimentation in a centrifuge sends denser particles to the bottom of the tube and lighter fluid toward the top.

q: A centrifugal pump is a hydraulic machine which converts mechanical energy into ____ energy by the use of centrifugal force.
e: A centrifugal pump is a hydraulic machine which converts mechanical energy into hydraulic energy by the use of centrifugal force. Centrifugal force is not a real interaction; it is an apparent outward effect of inertia in the rotating frame.

q: The rotating ____ in a centrifugal pump moves water or other fluids by using centrifugal force.
e: The rotating impeller in a centrifugal pump moves water or other fluids by using centrifugal force. Centrifugal force is not a real interaction; it is an apparent outward effect of inertia in the rotating frame.

q: The centrifugal action of a washing machine is used in ____ drying the clothes.
e: The centrifugal action of a washing machine is used in spin drying the clothes. Spin-drying uses the apparent outward throw of water; the real force on the water is inward from the drum.

q: In a washing machine, excess water is removed completely with the help of ____ force.
e: In a washing machine, excess water is removed completely with the help of centrifugal force. Centrifugal names the apparent outward effect in the rotating frame.

q: The centrifugal governor is a device used to measure and regulate the ____ of a machine, such as an engine.
e: The centrifugal governor is a device used to measure and regulate the speed of a machine, such as an engine. Speed is the magnitude of velocity.

q: The centrifugal governors consist of two balls of equal mass, which are attached to the ____.
e: The centrifugal governors consist of two balls of equal mass, which are attached to the arms. A centrifugal governor uses equal flying masses to measure and regulate engine speed.

q: As the engine is working, these balls also revolve around the ____ at a certain speed.
e: As the engine is working, these balls also revolve around the spindle at a certain speed. Governor balls are attached to the spindle and fly out as speed rises.

q: Centripetal force is directed towards the axis of rotation or centre of ____.
e: Centripetal force is directed towards the axis of rotation or centre of curvature. Centre of curvature is the geometric centre of the circular path.

q: Centrifugal force acts radially ____ from the centre of the circle.
e: Centrifugal force acts radially away from the centre of the circle. Centrifugal force is not a real interaction; it is an apparent outward effect of inertia in the rotating frame.

q: Centrifugal force results from the effect of ____.
e: Centrifugal force results from the effect of inertia. Centrifugal force is not a real interaction; it is an apparent outward effect of inertia in the rotating frame.

q: If a car is travelling through a curve, the centripetal force provided by the force of ____ between the tires and road allows the car to negotiate the turn.
e: If a car is travelling through a curve, the centripetal force provided by the force of friction between the tires and road allows the car to negotiate the turn. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r.

q: When a car in motion takes a sudden turn, passengers experience an ____ push.
e: When a car in motion takes a sudden turn, passengers experience an outward push. Outward is away from the centre, the apparent centrifugal sense.

q: A satellite orbiting a planet is supported by the ____ force.
e: A satellite orbiting a planet is supported by the centripetal force. Centripetal means toward the centre of the circle.

q: Removing excess water by spin drying clothes is accomplished with the help of ____ force.
e: Removing excess water by spin drying clothes is accomplished with the help of centrifugal force. Centrifugal names the apparent outward effect in the rotating frame.
